title: Hers vs FutureClinic: hair loss, menopause and weight care without the subscription
summary: Hers vs FutureClinic compares hair loss, menopause and weight care, covering Hers subscription costs, clinicians and FutureClinic's $40 doctor visit.
body_markdown:
Hers treats[hair loss](https://futureclinic.com/blog/hair-loss-treatment-online-without-a-subscription) ,[menopause](https://futureclinic.com/blog/menopause-treatment-online-hrt-from-a-doctor) , and weight management through ongoing subscription bundles and compounded formulas, fulfilled through its own and partner pharmacies. FutureClinic offers one-to-one care by message from a licensed physician, with no subscription required and prescriptions sent to the pharmacy you choose.


With FutureClinic, no form is approved in bulk. Instead, an individual physician reviews your full history, messages, and photos, makes each clinical call, and writes back with a plan and a Human Signature (a brief video or voice message your doctor records live just for you). After your first visit, you can return to the same doctor in the same chat whenever needed. Your physician is never restricted to one symptom either: a dermatologist managing your hair loss can address acne or eczema within their specialty, and because every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) , your care stays in one place.


## Who treats you, and why does the same doctor matter?


Hers treats weight, hair, perimenopause, menopause, skin, anxiety, and depression. On its menopause page, Hers notes that "A licensed provider trained in women's health will review your intake," and Hims & Hers'[2025 Form 10-K annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1773751/000177375126000022/hims-20251231.htm) states that care comes from "physicians,[nurse practitioners](https://futureclinic.com/blog/nurse-practitioner-vs-doctor-who-treats-you-online) , physician assistants, and behavioral health providers." In Hims' own[published provider lists](https://support.hims.com/hc/en-us/articles/44420848223003-Provider-Credentials-A-D) (updated July 23, 2026), about half of the clinicians (roughly 52%) are nurse practitioners and 48% are MDs or DOs. Keeping a clinician is not stated.


FutureClinic has over 300 doctors. The network includes primary care generalists and specialists spanning more than 60 specialties. We believe people's health deserves expert-level care, which is why every clinician on FutureClinic is a physician holding an MD, DO or MBBS degree, and never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant.


Staying in one ongoing chat with the same doctor, whether weeks or months pass between visits, is how you build trust, test options together, and track progress: adjusting a weight or hormone dose, swapping an irritating cream, or comparing this month's discounted lab result against last year's. Because FutureClinic sells no products and your physician earns nothing extra when ordering a test or writing a prescription, their sole incentive is helping you. With no house product line and no subscription needed to keep refills active, your doctor can prescribe whichever brand or generic treatment fits you (aside from controlled medicines) and send it to the pharmacy you choose, if your doctor decides it's right for you. Real care takes hours, not seconds: you receive replies typically within a few hours, and almost always the same day or the next.


Before signing up, it helps to ask yourself a simple question: do you want a Hers subscription bundle and its recurring membership requirements, or did you just want your own physician to talk to?


## How do Hers and FutureClinic compare?


Hers FutureClinic


**Who treats you** Physicians, NPs, PAs, behavioral health providers; keeping clinician not stated Physicians only (MD, DO or MBBS); keep the same doctor


**What you pay (as of October 2026)** Hair $12.67 to $35/mo; weight $39 month 1 then $149/mo plus medicine from $149/mo; menopause not stated $40 for best-fit doctor, or chosen doctor's price (typically $20 to $100); optional membership typically $25 to $100/mo


**Subscription required?** Yes No subscription required


**Where medicine comes from** Company and partner pharmacies (XeCare, Apostrophe, LillyDirect) The pharmacy you choose, including mail-order delivery


**What else they treat** App menu conditions; unrelated care not stated Other problems in their specialty; every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record


**How you reach them** App intake, messaging, video in some cases futureclinic.com or from your AI app (ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, Grok)


**What you get back** Plan and messages; reply time not stated Plan with Human Signature; replies typically within a few hours


## What does a year of treatment cost?


When comparing monthly rates, remember what a subscription model assumes: you must stay subscribed every month to continue getting refills. Per Hims & Hers' annual report, products are "sold to customers on a subscription basis" and "we do not accept payments from third-party payors." On[forhers.com](https://www.forhers.com/hair-loss/oral-minoxidil) as of October 2026, topical minoxidil starts at $12.67/month, oral minoxidil at $29/month ($348/year), and Hair Blends at $35/month. The[Hers menopause page](https://www.forhers.com/menopause) as of October 2026 shows "Begin free consult" with no price stated. In[Hims & Hers weight management](https://news.hims.com/newsroom/wegovy-r-pill-and-wegovy-r-pen-now-available-with-hims-hers) as of October 2026, members pay a program fee of $39 in the first month and $149/month after that ($1,678/year), charged separately from HSA/FSA-eligible brand GLP-1 cash prices starting at $149/month for the starting Wegovy pill dose; medication is unavailable without the membership, and cancelling stops the prescription.


On FutureClinic, no subscription is required. You pay $40 to be matched with the best-fit doctor, or pick a specific physician at their listed price, typically $20 to $100. When you take a stable medication and your physician judges a longer supply safe, one consultation can cover several months of a prescription at once, if your doctor decides it's right for you. We text you a link to route your prescription to the pharmacy you choose, including mail-order pharmacies that ship to your door, where health insurance may cover it or our discount coupon lowers the cash price. FutureClinic helps get a prior authorization when insurance needs one. For ongoing access, most physicians on FutureClinic also offer an optional[monthly membership](https://futureclinic.com/blog/telehealth-subscriptions-vs-paying-a-doctor-per-visit-yearly-cost) (typically $25 to $100 a month) that gives you unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time.
